title: LL-080R: logarithmic depth correction lowers classical-space coefficient at source coefficient4/5

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single LL-080R algorithm and complete configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^120; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), m=floor(4r/5)-10ceil(log2 r), dl=ceil(171r/200), hcap=floor(710557281r/1000000000), length-capped linear merges, free-frequency odd decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic recovery and all hard counters) outputs the full s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, failed attempts, discarded copies and aborts, total charged sequential work is T(N,s)=O(2^((331/200)sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n)=2^((331/200)sqrt n) has exact growth index1/2. Section14 proves absorption of the n^(9/2) work factor by the literal logarithmic depth reduction. This holds jointly with both space bounds, the source bound and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For the same LL-080R algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak classical memory on every execution branch is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((15655573/10000000) sqrt n)) bits, with an absolute constant, including depth-first merge tables and decoder records. The stronger main-branch bound is S_C = O(n^(3/2) 2^((1565557281/1000000000) sqrt n)). The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((15655573/10000000) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, quantum-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL-080R algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with an absolute constant, including the depth-first index registers and all ancillas. The envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL-080R algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, is O(2^((4/5) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is Q <= n Ccap + K = O(n^3 r^(-10) 2^((4/5)r)), with Ccap and K defined in proof.md. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((4/5) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work and memory bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL-080R algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
